articleTitle: Principles of Solving the Space Monitoring Problem by Multirotors Swarm
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this paper space patrolling models, methods and algorithms are describing on the example of the problem of a human face detection in a pre-known territory solving by a swarm of multirotors. Several key approaches to the solution of this problem were selected, the effectiveness of each was tested under various experimental conditions, the limits of applicability of these approaches were found.

articleTitle: Modification of the Scheme of Division of Asmuth-Bloom Data with the Application of the Method of Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The article discusses the scheme of Asmuth-Bloom data separation and its modification using fractal geometry as a coding function, as well as a numerical method for computing data parts using the modified Asmuth-Bloom data separation scheme. The proposed modification allows simultaneously divide and encode the image without applying additional algorithms and, therefore, without increasing computational complexity.

articleTitle: A Modification of the Hybrid Projection Method for Electrodynamical Analysis of Inhomogeneous Dielectric Cylinder with Arbitrary Cross Section
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The 2D problem of E-polarized plane electromagnetic wave scattering by an inhomogeneous dielectric cylinder with arbitrary cross section is considered. A modification of the hybrid projection method is developed for its solution on the basis of projection matching of the fields on the boundaries of circular cylindrical regions introduced in the consideration, projection of the Helmholtz equation for inhomogeneous region on the Fourier harmonics, and application of the one-dimensional method of finite elements in projection form to the derived ordinary differential equations for reduction of the latter to an algebraic system with block-banded matrix. Some results obtained for a homogeneous cylinder of elliptical cross section are compared to appropriate results obtained using the method of auxiliary sources, and the results obtained for a homogeneous cylinder of square cross section are compared to appropriate results available in the literature. Performance of a half-cylindrical Maxwell fish-eye lens is also calculated and discussed.

articleTitle: Fast Power-of-Two RNS Scaling Algorithm for Large Dynamic Ranges
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper presents a new efficient algorithm for scaling by power of two in the residue number system (RNS). It focuses on arbitrary moduli sets with large dynamic ranges. In this algorithm, in order to determine the remainder when dividing the number to be scaled by the scaling factor, an interval estimation of the RNS representation is used. The proposed algorithm requires only machine-precision integer and floating-point operations, and is well parallelized. The algorithm is implemented for CPU, as well as for GPU using CUDA C language.

articleTitle: An Overview of Spatial Modulation Techniques for Millimeter Wave MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The emerging of millimeter wave (mmWave) communications has been widely predicted to revolutionize the traditional communications. On one hand, the large bandwidth provided by mmWave is orders of magnitudes larger than that provided by current microwave communications, which therefore supports much higher throughput as well as massive connectivity. On the other hand, the small wavelength of mmWave signals facilitates the application of massive antennas, thus benefiting from the powerful multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) beamforming and other MIMO signal processing techniques. However, mmWave-MIMO systems often suffer from prohibitive power consumption due to the massive antennas and radio frequency (RF) chains. Spatial modulation (SM) techniques have been proposed as a low-complexity, low-power-consumption MIMO candidate. More importantly, the idea of incorporating SM techniques into mmWave-MIMO systems has been proved effective for reducing the number of radio frequency (RF) chains, to which many research efforts have been devoted. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the combination of SM and mmWave communications, with a special emphasis on the hybrid beamforming regimes for SM-motivated mmWave-MIMO systems

Author Keywords: Multiple-input multiple-output; spatial modulation; generalized spatial modulation; millimeter wave; hybrid

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Complex Filtering Methods for PAPR Reduction of OFDM Signals with Low Computational Complexity
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the reconfigurable complex filtering techniques based on the Tone Reservation (TR) set and data bearing sub-carriers in the time-domain and in the frequency-domain to reduce the Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) of OFDM signals. The simulation results of the proposed methods for 16-QAM and 64-QAM modulation are presented. These results show that PAPR of OFDM signals is significantly reduced (about 6.6 dB), and OFDM signals can reach the desired amplitude level after 2-4 iterations.

articleTitle: Code-Based Cryptosystems Evolution
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper describes the original linear code-based cryptosystem and shows how it evolves after successful structural-based attacks have been discovered. All existing modifications of the original Niederreiter public-key algorithm have been classified based on improvements and classified accordingly common characteristics and variety of parameters. Based on the analysis authors approximates further code-based systems movement towards the development of real-life implementations and possible standarts.

articleTitle: LINC Efficiency Improvement for Multichannel Signal Amplification
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: LINC amplifier efficiency is estimated. Amplifier simultaneously applies the combination of two methods to improve the efficiency of signal components combining. Evaluation is performed by simulation with multichannel signal samples transmitted through the amplifier. The results show the gain in efficiency compared to using one of the methods.

articleTitle: Smart Concurrent Learning Scheme for 5G Network: QoS-Aware Radio Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The continuous performance race led wireless industry to a ubiquitous adoption of heterogeneous architecture with small cells. Although, the extreme densification offers the largest increase in the network capacity, it also challenges more valuable system metrics like quality of service (QoS) for users with various traffic types. While previously used to boost capacity in the cellular system, radio resource management schemes now need to be refocused to address the requirements of the next generation services. In this paper, we propose a novel power profile construction framework designed specifically for scenarios with multiple traffic types and a smart way to adopt it to a distributed learning algorithm. The main goal is to provide each cell with the ability to make its decision autonomously while taking into account the QoS metrics of the surrounding cells. We illustrate the application of this distributed learning strategy for the subband allocation and propose several mechanisms to improve the convergence speed in the absence of communication. To address the arising convergence challenge we propose to additionally enhance the proposed algorithm with a smart model fitting stage. Taking advantage of this ideas, we were able to properly utilize flexibility and meet the strict requirements of machine learning algorithm for QoS scenarios. The performances of the proposed method are evaluated in the case of Long Term Evolution (LTE-A) setup and compared to a number of traditional resource allocation schemes. System level simulations show that it achieves a considerable improvement in system performance for heterogeneous deployment, without compromising the quality of service of the overall system.

articleTitle: The α-β Filter for Tracking Maneuvering Objects with LFM Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: A linear frequency modulated (LFM) waveform is widely used for tracking moving objects. However, the range-Doppler coupling of LFM waveform can both improve and worsen the track accuracy in a radial coordinate. Besides that, while tracking maneuvering objects, an α-β-filter develops a lag error in its estimates and position estimate variance does not accurately represent actual position error. Therefore, in this paper, the features of α-β-filter processing measurements from LFM waveforms are studied. Analysis of total variance which equals to the sum of the position estimate variance and position lag error is carried out. An optimal relation between α and β, at which the total variance reaches a minimum, is derived. In doing so, using this α-β-relationship and α-β-filter stability conditions, a feasible region of the filter parameters is derived in dependence on the range-Doppler coupling coefficient.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Determining Optimum Operation Tolerances of Memristor-Based Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The article contains the results obtained by applying a general approach, which has been developed by the authors, to determining optimum values (reaching the specified level or receiving the maximum possible value) of operation tolerances of high performance memristor-based artificial neural networks (ANNM) through the use of the methodologies of system analysis and simulation modeling. Using this approach the authors have devised and programmatically implemented an algorithm aimed to solve the stated-above problem by means of varying the digit capacity of input information. The operation of a two-layer feedforward ANNM, taught to detect the squitter of a ADS-B signal with noises and interference in the background, has been used as an example during the research. In the course of the research, the authors have developed a general mathematical model of the system and a general modelling algorithm. They have also carried out simulation modelling, defined and optimized the tolerances for the parameters of neurons of the synthesized ANNM.

Author Keywords: signal detection with noises and interference in the background

articleTitle: SAND-Inspired Cross-Layer Approach for CCTV in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this work, we propose an approach to deploy and manage resources in a surveillance system, based on cellular technologies. In such a system, on one hand, the data from CCTV cameras should be reliably delivered with as higher quality as possible within several seconds after they were generated to enable near real-time surveillance. On the other hand, the Web traffic, which is generated in public cellular networks shall be delivered with the same quality as if there were no CCTV at all. In the paper, we propose an approach of how to design such a system based on the 5G technology and how to organize transmission to satisfy the described requirements and provide near-optimal quality of the generated video.

articleTitle: Wavelet-Based Video Coding: Modem Implementations and Prospects of Coding Efficiency Increase
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Discrete wavelet transform (DWT) have found a practical use in multiple applications of digital signal processing including image compression. Despite a set of advantages, DWT is still weakly used in modern video compression technique and systems. Here an observation of DWT usage prospects is presented for video coding in terms of multichannel wavelet video codec implementation.

articleTitle: On the Nested Family of LDPC Codes Based on Golomb Rulers
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this paper we present a new ensemble of Low- Density Parity-Check codes (LDPC Codes) based on modular Golomb rulers and permutation matrices. We suggest a designing rule for these codes that allows obtaining a nested family of LDPC codes with wide range of rates from one matrix of lowest rate code. Moreover, the regular way that we apply to construct our codes allows describing parity-check matrices with minimal number of parameters. The simulation results in the case of transmission via AWGN channel with QAM-4 modulation are presented.

articleTitle: Design and Research of the Algorithms for Recognition of Axisymmetric Radar Objects on the Basis of Polarization Signs
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Algorithms for recognition of axisymmetric radar objects on the basis of polarization signs with the use of Stokes parameters and those of a two-dipole model (TDM) to be applied in a complex of recognition algorithms have been developed. The results of algorithm modeling at the movement of objects of observation on the extra-atmospheric site of a trajectory are presented. The results of research to define the most informative group of polarization signs are given.

articleTitle: Architecting Automated Control System of Above Ground Transport System of H-Bahn Type
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The article describes the project of construction of automatic control system of above ground transport by H-Bahn technology. Key functional requirements for the system control of above ground transport system are formulated. Architectures of control systems of existing transport systems are analyzed. An overall structural scheme of a system of automated transport system control of H-Bahn type is proposed and its functioning described.

articleTitle: A Statistical Construction of Lyapunov Function in the Problems for Setting Stability of a Controlled Dynamical System
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This article presents a statistical synthesis of stability conditions to multifactoriate uncertainties for a controlled dynamical system, and introduces a construction of Lyapunov function according to a statistical sample for evaluating the stability of controlled dynamical system through an example of UAV's model. The stability evaluation for a guided dynamical system (in a UAV's example) is introduced with the statistical approach to formulating Lyapunov stability conditions.

articleTitle: Building Mathematical Model for Restoring Processes Tree during Container Live Migration
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper provides an attempt to solve the problem of restoring Linux processes tree during container live migration by creation a mathematical model describing operations, which are performed with container processes tree while container works. During live migration of the container, the state of each process in the container processes tree is saved and then the tree is restored on another node. Restoring includes determining the order of operations that should be performed in the container to create processes tree with the same state, which is a complex operation. Errors during it make future behavior of the container unpredictable and can cause serious issues. In this paper, matrix representation of processes tree will be introduced and a mathematical model of operations on processes will be created.

articleTitle: Power Analysis: Simplified Template Attack on Exclusive Disjunction Operation
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The new method of power analysis attack using classification algorithms against microchips introduced. Methodology of generating simplified templates and collecting valuable signal described. Global parameters of classifiers optimized for better accuracy. Estimates for computational complexity and time consumption provided. Approaches for potential enhancements of performance suggested.

articleTitle: New Rank Codes with Efficient Decoding
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Linear maximum rank distance (MRD) codes in vector representation for all parameters are known for many years [3], [4]. There exist fast decoding algorithms to correct rank errors and rank erasures for these codes [3], [5], [6], [7]. Recently, Sheekey [8] and other researches [9], [10], [11], [12] proposed new families of the vector MRD codes. No decoding algorithms were still described. In this paper, generator and parity-check matrices are constructed for a few new codes. Our contribution is a new construction of the vector MRD codes based on modification of codes from [3]. Efficient decoding algorithms are described.

articleTitle: Decoding of DMR-Standard Block Codes on the 1967BH034 Processor
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The article describes the results of the decoding block codes using 1967BH034 signal processor. The algorithms provide optimal or close to optimal decoding performance, with effective implementation of the selected signal processor.

articleTitle: Assignment of Semantics Calculations in Invariants of Similarity
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In the theory of similarity, the analysis of equations and the analysis of dimensions are distinguished [1-5]. In this regard, there are two possible ways of specifying the alphabet of the language of representing the semantics of partially correct computations in similarity invariants.

articleTitle: On Conditional Probabilities of Output Sequences for Permutation-Based PRNGs
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: We investigate and compare several constructions of pseudorandom number generators based on block ciphers in counter mode. An idealized models of those constructions are considered, where the block ciphers are assumed to be random permutations. For these models we compute lower and upper bounds for conditional probabilities for the next element to appear given a prefix. We also consider a few criteria to evaluate generators output sequence and then compare generators to each other by one of these criteria.

articleTitle: Analysis of 1D-Periodic Phased Array of Flanged Rectangular Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: A model of ID-periodic phased array of flanged rectangular waveguides is discussed. This model is reduced to a system of integral-algebraic equations. Integral part was reduced to algebraic equations using piecewise constant approximation. The system obtained was solved numerically. Some results including antenna gain, reflection coefficient and axial ratio are obtained and discussed.

articleTitle: Method Forming Signals for High-Speed Radio Access Systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Communication systems built on the basis of soft difinion radio (SDR) architecture using Cognitive radio (CRS) algorithms are assigned greater expectations. However, signals, which are used in today's modern radio communication systems (signals with orthogonal frequency multiplexing Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplex (OFDM)) have a number of shortcomings, one of which is the high side lobe level of individual subcarriers that does not allow the provision of potential spectral effectiveness of high-speed radio access systems. The article describes a new method developed, which is based on the use of special shaping functions with good localization of energy in the frequency domain, which provides a rapid decline in side lobe spectrum of the generated signal in the specified time duration of the signal. Using of this method allows for the generation of a signal not only with empty areas in the spectrum of a signal of a certain width for adaptation to complex electromagnetic conditions, but also a low level of noise interference in these areas, that cannot be obtained using signals from orthogonal frequency multiplexing.

articleTitle: EEG Analysis Based on the Empirical Mode Decomposition for Detection of Mental Activity
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The article describes a new approach to the analysis of frequency components of electroencephalograms for the determination of human psychic activity. To solve the set problems, we used the method of empirical mode decomposition implemented in Matlab and R environment. To assess a human mental state (before/after mental impact, or stress), the estimation of signal empirical modes is used as a decisive rule for setting a diagnosis. The research results of more than 400 signals of electroencephalograms showed a high accuracy of a signal ratio to a mental disorder: an error of the 1st kind is 2%, an error of the second kind is 5%.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Corporate Network Based on Software-Defined Infrastructure and Network Function Virtualization
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: There is a problem of creating the models of modern software-defined and software-configurable infrastructure components. Many simulation platforms do not have tools for implementing such models. This paper describes the features of corporate virtualized network infrastructures. The approach to creating an abstracted model of a part of the infrastructure based on virtual prototype studies is considered, a simulation scheme for a switch and a controller for software-defined infrastructure is proposed.

articleTitle: The Methods of Solving Tasks Measuring Characteristics of the Laser Beam Radiations Using Quadra Copter
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The method of laser beam angular divergence measurement with the help of Quadra copter is suggested. Assumption of Gaussian angular distribution of power density was used. Experimental dates are presented. Theoretical estimations of proposed methods are confirmed by experimental results.

articleTitle: Accelerating Simulation of Future Processors with Compiler and Microcode Assist
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Pre-silicon software development approach requires fast simulation of future hardware to run full software stacks far ahead of silicon availability. Wind River(R) Simics(R) virtual platform framework we use relies on Intel(R) VT-x technology to accelerate simulation of Intel targets using Intel host processors. In the case of Intel Control-flow Enforcement Technology (CET), standard Intel VT-x based direct execution technique turned out to be inapplicable due to the nature of the new extension. To achieve usable performance, we created a novel solution based on microcode patching. This approach provided the performance needed to successfully enable pre-silicon work on CET. Simics with microcode assists was used to enable CET support in several important software stacks, including operating systems, compilers and databases.

articleTitle: Method for Detection of Failures in Complex Process Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: At present automatic control systems and control of distributed power facilities are complex technical systems, in which include large number of elements and have complex structure. Automated system of management of technical process (ASMTP) is a group of solutions of hardware and software designed to automate control of technological equipment in industrial enterprises.

articleTitle: Markov's Model of the Different-Priority Traffic Routing Control in a Sensor Node
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The possibilities of and conditions for using Markov model are determined when describing the work of sensor unit in controlling measurable data traffic routing. The mathematical formulation of radio channels having different distribution capacity between communication lines that represent transmission routes with different-priority information in wireless sensor networks problem is developed. The criterion for solving the problem is the minimization of losses in service information flows in the communication line, which has the lowest indices of interference immunity and message transmission efficiency. An algorithm for solving the particular problem of fixing five channels with different capacities for three communication lines with various admissible values of the delay in traffic servicing is given.

articleTitle: Development Trends and International Standardization of Broadcasting Service
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The main directions of modern broadcast service are transition from analogue to digital sound, multimedia, and television broadcasting, advanced quality of audio and video content, convergence of various means for broadcast content delivery for providing the user with maximum possible content quality. The results of the last ITU-R Study Group 6 block meeting are presented.

articleTitle: Cardinality of Subspace Multicomponent Codes
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper is devoted to multicomponent subspace codes with zero prefix (MZP). The construction is described. The codes are divided into two parts. The first part contains the codes which code distance is not maximal. The second part contains of the codes with maximal code distance, so called partial spreads. It connects with different ways to estimate the upper bounds of cardinality. Cardinality for codes is calculated for different parameters. The obtained values are compared with the corresponding upper bounds. It is shown that the cardinality of the codes from the first part does not coincides with the upper bound. The cardinality of the partial spreads coincides or almost coincides with the upper bound. It depends on code dimension. By definition, efficiency is defined as ratio of the cardinality of the code for given parameters to the upper bound at the same parameters.

articleTitle: Multiobjective Optimization of Greenhouse Gas Emissions Enhancing the Quality of Service for Urban Public Transport Timetabling
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper presents a multiobjective cellular genetic algorithm to determine bus timetables using multiple vehicle types, considering restrictions of government agencies for public transport systems in the context of smart cities. The first objective is to reduce the greenhouse gas emissions by the minimization of number of vehicles wasting fuel transiting with low ridership. The second one is to minimize number of passengers that cannot move in a certain time-period increasing vehicles overload and waiting time. A set of non-dominated solutions represents different assignments of vehicles covering a given set of trips in a defined route. Our experimental analysis shows a competitive performance of the proposed algorithm in terms of convergence and diversity. It outperforms non-dominated sets provided by NSGA-n.

articleTitle: RoC Prediction for Bi-Objective Cost-QoS Optimization of Cloud VoIP Call Allocations
publicationTitle: 2017 IVth International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this paper, we present cloud VoIP scheduling strategies to provide appropriate levels of quality of service to users, and cost to VoIP service providers. This bi-objective problem is reasonable and representative for real installations and applications. We conduct comprehensive simulation on real data of sixty four strategies with dynamic prediction of the load. We show that our prediction rule that consider the number of Virtual Machines (VMs) running in the system improves the efficiency of traditional rate of change algorithm. It provides suitable quality of service and lower cost. Variations of VM startup time delays permit to evaluate the prediction rules under different scenarios and assess the robustness of all strategies.
